title: Auf dem Markt — at the market
summary: Buying bread and apples. Numbers, prices and the accusative case doing its quiet work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Guten Morgen. Was darf es sein?
lines.translation: Good morning. What can I get you?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ich hätte gern ein Brot, bitte.
lines.translation: I would like a loaf of bread, please.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ja, ein Kilo Äpfel. Was kosten die?
lines.translation: Yes, a kilo of apples. What do they cost?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gut, dann nehme ich ein Kilo.
lines.translation: Good, I'll take a kilo then.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Das macht zusammen fünf Euro dreißig.
lines.translation: That comes to five euros thirty altogether.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Here you are. Keep the change.

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: Thank you. Have a good day!

vocabulary.meaning: what can I get you? — the standard shop greeting
I would like — politer than ich will, and the phrase to learn first
keep the change (literally: that's right as it is)

questions.q: What do the apples cost per kilo?
Which phrase did she use to order politely?
questions.explain: Ich hätte gern — the subjunctive, and the normal polite way to ask for something.
